# Brahmanimantanika Sutta (MN 49 (PTS MN i 326))

**ID:** MN 49 (PTS MN i 326)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Brahmanimantanika Sutta
**PTS:** MN i 326
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

During this encounter, the Buddha engages in a dramatic contest of supernormal power and wits against both Baka Brahmā and Māra the Evil One, who possesses an attendant in Brahmā's assembly to defend the sanctity of worldly existence against the Buddha's teaching of *nibbāna* [Flores 2008; Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995; Hazra 1994; Bingenheimer 2013]. The text is particularly notable in doctrinal discussions for containing the famous phrase *viññāṇaṁ anidassanaṁ anantam* ("featureless" or "unmanifested consciousness") [Ñāṇananda 2009; Sharf 2014].

 DharmaNexus matches confirm strong cross-language alignment between MN 49 and the *Madhyamāgama* (ZH_T01_0026_019) as well as the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* from Subaši [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, the prose opening and episode correspond closely to the *Brahma Saṁyutta* (SN 6) and the *Brahmā Baka Jātaka* (Ja 405) [Bodhi 2003; DharmaNexus], while extensive textual reuse is also detected with the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), *Mūlapariyāya Sutta* (MN 1), *Kevaṭṭa Sutta* (DN 11), and *Brahmajāla Sutta* (DN 1) [DharmaNexus].
